intro: This week's five themes: Alzheimer's pipeline crowding, atopic dermatitis's first dual-mechanism bispecific, a colorectal-cancer vaccine safety halt alongside new China-origin entrants, combination logic and live bacterial therapeutics spreading into new indications, and an RNAi-vs-antisense safety comparison in cardiology.

narratives.headline: Alzheimer's pipeline crowding: three new pre-efficacy entrants this week, including a head-to-head amyloid trial
narratives.detail: Three new pre-efficacy Alzheimer's programs entered the tracked universe this week: a fourth compound in one major sponsor's own anti-amyloid franchise, tested head-to-head against its other amyloid mechanisms under a single master trial design; a second-generation antibody-like compound from a second sponsor moving into an early symptomatic population; and a first oral small-molecule modulator of amyloid oligomers from a smaller specialist sponsor. It's the largest one-day jump in early-stage amyloid programs logged this year within the tracked set, though an external registry pull across all amyloid-directed mechanisms would be needed to call the space more or less crowded industry-wide.

narratives.headline: Atopic dermatitis gets a skin-barrier/IL-13 bispecific and a kinase inhibitor moving over from rheumatoid arthritis
narratives.detail: Atopic dermatitis added a first-in-class bispecific this week pairing a skin-barrier-repair mechanism with an interleukin-13-blocking mechanism, the first such combination logged in this indication, alongside a second, mechanistically undisclosed China-origin entrant. A third addition extends a class this note has tracked broadening across skin and joint disease for over a year: an oral inhibitor of two intracellular signalling kinases, previously tracked here only in rheumatoid arthritis, is now being tested in atopic dermatitis for the first time. Together they mark dermatology's entry into dual-mechanism combination logic already established in oncology.

narratives.headline: Personalized colorectal-cancer vaccine program halted after more deaths on treatment than control in adjuvant use
narratives.detail: A major sponsor's individualized cancer-vaccine program in colorectal cancer was discontinued this week after an independent safety monitoring board flagged more deaths in the treatment arm than the control arm during adjuvant, disease-free use, a signal specific to that minimal-residual-disease setting rather than a verdict on personalized cancer vaccines generally. Separately, colorectal cancer added two China-origin combination entrants: an oral compound engineered to work around a resistance mechanism common to an older targeted-therapy class paired with an existing antibody backbone, and a bispecific already on a priority regulatory track elsewhere for a rare neuroendocrine cancer, now tested in colorectal cancer for the first time. Both layer onto a landscape already crowded with targeted-combination and antibody-drug-conjugate approaches.

narratives.headline: Combination-drug logic keeps spreading beyond oncology as Crohn's logs its first oral live bacterial therapeutic
narratives.detail: Dual/multi-mechanism combination logic kept spreading beyond oncology this week: a bispecific pairing a skin-barrier-repair mechanism with a cytokine-blocking mechanism entered dermatology for the first time, and a checkpoint-times-costimulatory bispecific already progressing toward a first approval in a rare cancer moved into a much larger, common solid tumor for the first time. Separately, Crohn's disease logged its first oral live bacterial therapeutic in the tracked universe: an engineered probiotic-style strain designed to express a therapeutic surface protein, now entering early safety testing. Both read as read-across of already-validated logic into new settings rather than a new mechanism class, and the live-bacterial data point is too thin (small, safety-only trial) to call a modality trend yet.

narratives.headline: RNAi lipid-lowering candidate posts a stronger safety read than its antisense rival at a major cardiology congress
narratives.detail: A lipid-lowering RNAi asset extended its standing comparative thread against the leading antisense competitor in the same target class: at a major cardiology congress, the RNAi candidate reported a stronger safety and tolerability read than the antisense drug across two late-stage severe-hypertriglyceridemia trials, with comparable efficacy. This is the first time the comparison has surfaced specifically on safety and tolerability rather than efficacy alone, building on an earlier positive late-stage readout from the same sponsor pair already framed as a head-to-head story. The indication sits outside this note's core tracked set, so it's logged as ecosystem-only platform color rather than a clinical-layer update.
